unit: Unit XVI — Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
title: Electrophilic Substitutions of Phenol: Kolbe, Reimer-Tiemann, & Redox
topics: 7.1 Kolbe’s Reaction: Sodium Phenoxide + CO₂ (400 K, 4–7 atm) ──[H⁺]──► Salicylic Acid (Precursor for Aspirin)
7.2 Reimer-Tiemann Reaction: Phenol + CHCl₃ + NaOH at 340 K ──► Salicylaldehyde
Active Electrophile in Reimer-Tiemann: Dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂, neutral 6-electron species via α-elimination)
7.3 Bromination: Br₂ in CS₂ (273 K) ──► p-Bromophenol Major vs Br₂/H₂O ──► 2,4,6-Tribromophenol (White Precipitate)
Oxidation to 1,4-Benzoquinone & Neutral FeCl₃ Qualitative Complex Test (Violet [Fe(OPh)₆]³⁻)
quickSummary: Kolbe's reaction: Phenoxide + CO₂ ──► Salicylic acid (acetylated to Aspirin). Reimer-Tiemann: Phenol + CHCl₃ + NaOH ──► Salicylaldehyde via neutral Dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂). Bromine in CS₂ gives p-bromophenol; bromine water gives 2,4,6-tribromophenol white ppt. Oxidation yields 1,4-benzoquinone. Neutral FeCl₃ gives violet [Fe(OPh)₆]³⁻.
summary: Master Kolbe's carboxylation, Reimer-Tiemann formylation, bromination selectivity, and phenol redox reactions.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PHENOL ELECTROPHILIC REACTIONS
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                             ▼                             ▼
   KOLBE'S REACTION             REIMER-TIEMANN REACTION        NITRATION & BROMINATION
   Phenoxide $+ \text{CO}_2 \xrightarrow{400\text{ K, 4–7 atm}}$ Phenol $+ \text{CHCl}_3 + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow$  ├── Dil. $\text{HNO}_3 \to o/p$-Nitrophenol
   $\xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \mathbf{\text{Salicylic Acid}}$    Electrophile: **Dichlorocarbene ($:\text{CCl}_2$)**└── $\text{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O} \to \mathbf{2,4,6\text{-Tribromophenol}\downarrow}$
                                └── Yields **Salicylaldehyde**     (White Precipitate)
conceptBreakdown.content:
- **Kolbe's Reaction**: Sodium phenoxide reacts with $\text{CO}_2$ ($400\text{ K, 4–7 atm}$) to form Salicylic Acid (acetylated with acetic anhydride to make **Aspirin**).
- **Reimer-Tiemann Reaction**: Phenol reacts with $\text{CHCl}_3$ and $\text{NaOH}$ to yield Salicylaldehyde via the neutral 6-electron electrophile **Dichlorocarbene ($:\text{CCl}_2$)**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.3 Bromination, Oxidation, & FeCl₃ Qualitative Test
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.3 Bromination, Oxidation, & FeCl₃ Qualitative Test
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PHENOL BROMINATION & QUALITATIVE TESTS:

• Br₂ in CS₂ (273 K):   Phenol + Br₂ ──► p-Bromophenol (Major) + o-Bromophenol
• Bromine Water:        Phenol + 3Br₂(aq) ──► 2,4,6-Tribromophenol ↓ (White Precipitate)
• Chromic Acid:         Phenol + Na₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄ ──► 1,4-Benzoquinone (Conjugated Diketone)
• Neutral FeCl₃ Test:   Phenol + FeCl₃ ──► [Fe(OPh)₆]³⁻ (Intense Violet / Purple Solution)
conceptBreakdown.content: Water polarizes phenol into phenoxide, causing polybromination to $2,4,6$-tribromophenol white precipitate. In non-polar $\text{CS}_2$, monobromination dominates ($p$-bromophenol major).

quickRevision: Kolbe's reaction makes Salicylic acid using CO₂ and phenoxide.
Salicylic acid + Acetic Anhydride gives Aspirin (Acetylsalicylic acid).
Reimer-Tiemann uses CHCl₃ + NaOH to make Salicylaldehyde via :CCl₂.
Br₂/CS₂ gives p-bromophenol; Br₂/H₂O gives 2,4,6-tribromophenol white ppt.
Neutral FeCl₃ gives an intense violet color ([Fe(OPh)₆]³⁻).
